ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The rotor of a sinusoidal AC generator is a square coil with $n=100$ turns and side length $L=20\mathrm{cm}$. It is placed in a uniform magnetic field with magnetic induction $B=0.5\mathrm{T}$. Under the action of an external force, it rotates uniformly around an axis perpendicular to the direction of the magnetic field at an angular velocity of $\omega=100\pi$ (rad/s). Timing starts when the plane of the coil is perpendicular to the direction of the magnetic field. The resistance of the coil is $r=1\Omega$, and the external circuit resistance is $R=99\Omega$.

1. Write the expression for the instantaneous value of alternating current; do not add any other content.
2. The power consumed by the external resistor; do not add any other content.
3. The power of external forces.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The rotor of a sinusoidal AC generator is a square coil with $n=100$ turns and side length $L=20\mathrm{cm}$. It is placed in a uniform magnetic field with magnetic induction $B=0.5\mathrm{T}$. Under the action of an external force, it rotates uniformly around an axis perpendicular to the direction of the magnetic field at an angular velocity of $\omega=100\pi\,\mathrm{rad/s}$. Timing starts when the plane of the coil is perpendicular to the direction of the magnetic field. The resistance of the coil is $r=1\Omega$, and the external circuit resistance is $R=99\Omega$. 1. Write the expression for the instantaneous value of alternating current; do not add any other content. 2. The power consumed by the external resistor; do not add any other content. 3. The power of external forces.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Calculate according to the specified method. The coil area S=L^2=(0.20)^2=0.04 m^2. At the beginning of timing, the plane of the coil is perpendicular to the direction of the magnetic field, therefore the normal of the coil is parallel to the direction of the magnetic field, and the initial magnetic flux is maximum, so the total flux linkage is Φ_n=nBS cos(ωt). According to Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the induced electromotive force e=-dΦ_n/dt=nBSω sin(ωt). Substituting n=100, B=0.5 T, S=0.04 m^2, ω=100π rad/s, the peak value of the electromotive force is E_0=100×0.5×0.04×100π=200π V. The total resistance R+r=99+1=100 Ω, therefore the peak current I_0=E_0/(R+r)=200π/100=2π A≈6.28 A, so i=6.28 sin(100πt) A. The effective value I_rms=I_0/√2, therefore I_rms^2=I_0^2/2=(2π)^2/2=2π^2. The average power consumed by the external resistance P_R=I_rms^2 R=2π^2×99=198π^2 W. The external force power is equal to the total average electric power required to maintain uniform rotation, that is, P_ext=I_rms^2(R+r)=2π^2×100=200π^2 W.
